cause_assessments.reason: The coherent original frame records audio.choice label as “✓, Wi-Fi only” while the visible wording is complete. The frozen Android observer walks unmerged descendants and synthesizes its label by concatenating native Text (NativeObserverTest.kt lines 88–89 and 137); production source lines 199–208 clears semantics on the decorative Box. The raw strict label failure is retained. These inputs do not export the merged accessibility-service label, so they do not resolve observation aggregation versus an actual component accessibility-label defect. Host gutters and paint sampling do not explain this text discrepancy.

The original collector records “✓, Wi-Fi only” by synthesizing a label from unmerged descendant Text (NativeObserverTest.kt raw() at line 89 and label() at line 137), rather than an Android accessibility-service label. The production choice explicitly clears semantics on the decorative mark Box (OfflineAudioTourPanel.kt lines 200–205) and exposes selected separately at lines 189–191. The visible Wi-Fi only text is complete. Preserve the strict native F; this unmerged-label construction supports an observation cause and does not establish a product accessibility-label defect or a TalkBack pass.

cause_assessments.reason: The coherent original frame records audio.choice label as “✓, Wi-Fi only” while the visible wording is complete. The frozen Android observer walks unmerged descendants and synthesizes its label by concatenating native Text (NativeObserverTest.kt lines 88–89 and 137); production source lines 199–208 clears semantics on the decorative Box. The raw strict label failure is retained. These inputs do not export the merged accessibility-service label, so they do not resolve observation aggregation versus an actual component accessibility-label defect. Host gutters and paint sampling do not explain this text discrepancy.

The original collector records “✓, Wi-Fi only” by synthesizing a label from unmerged descendant Text (NativeObserverTest.kt raw() at line 89 and label() at line 137), rather than an Android accessibility-service label. The production choice explicitly clears semantics on the decorative mark Box (OfflineAudioTourPanel.kt lines 200–205) and exposes selected separately at lines 189–191. The visible Wi-Fi only text is complete. Preserve the strict native F; this unmerged-label construction supports an observation cause and does not establish a product accessibility-label defect or a TalkBack pass.

cause_assessments.reason: The coherent original frame records audio.choice label as “✓, Wi-Fi only” while the visible wording is complete. The frozen Android observer walks unmerged descendants and synthesizes its label by concatenating native Text (NativeObserverTest.kt lines 88–89 and 137); production source lines 199–208 clears semantics on the decorative Box. cause_assessments.reason: The coherent original frame records audio.choice label as “✓, Wi-Fi only” while the visible wording is complete. The frozen Android observer walks unmerged descendants and synthesizes its label by concatenating native Text (NativeObserverTest.kt lines 88–89 and 137); production source lines 199–208 clears semantics on the decorative Box. The raw strict label failure is retained. These inputs do not export the merged accessibility-service label, so they do not resolve observation aggregation versus an actual component accessibility-label defect. Host gutters and paint sampling do not explain this text discrepancy.

The original collector records “✓, Wi-Fi only” by synthesizing a label from unmerged descendant Text (NativeObserverTest.kt raw() at line 89 and label() at line 137), rather than an Android accessibility-service label. The production choice explicitly clears semantics on the decorative mark Box (OfflineAudioTourPanel.kt lines 200–205) and exposes selected separately at lines 189–191. The visible Wi-Fi only text is complete. Preserve the strict native F; this unmerged-label construction supports an observation cause and does not establish a product accessibility-label defect or a TalkBack pass.

source_datum.value: Harbor museum: voices of the working port

Begin beside the old harbor gate and listen for the bell that once announced a vessel arriving at the quay. The introduction describes how workers coordinated a busy waterfront before radios became part of everyday port life.

Walk toward the long rope-making bench and compare the tools displayed above it. This chapter follows a small team preparing a heavy line, with pauses that let you examine the fibers and the worn wooden handles nearby.

Stand beside the half-built hull and look along the curve of its ribs. The shipwright describes choosing timber, checking a joint, and teaching an apprentice to notice a small gap before the outer planks were fitted.

The market gallery brings together sellers, carriers, and the people who repaired baskets at the end of the day. Listen beside the weighing table, then look for the chalk price board before continuing into the next room.

At the signal cabinet, the narrator explains why a clear message mattered in poor weather. Short examples describe the flags and lamps without requiring you to identify every symbol, so you can listen while examining the original equipment.

Pause near the engine model and follow the route from the boiler to the propeller shaft. A mechanic recalls the rhythm of routine checks and explains how the crew recognized a change in the sound of a working engine.

The writing desk holds copies of letters sent home during long trips. This chapter reads brief passages about ordinary meals, changing weather, and missing family, with quiet intervals that give you time to inspect the handwriting on display.

Finish at the large window overlooking the present harbor. The final voices discuss new jobs and familiar landmarks, inviting you to compare the view outside with the historical photographs on the adjacent wall before you leave the gallery.
